# shop.

A small store for considered everyday goods. Node.js 22, Express 4, plain JavaScript, esbuild, and JSON-file storage. All API money values are integer cents.

## Install, run and build

Run `npm install --no-audit --no-fund`, then `npm run build` and `npm start`. Visit http://localhost:3000. Set `PORT` to choose another port, for example `PORT=8080 npm start`.

Run `npm test` for the entire node:test suite. Each test uses an isolated temporary data directory and a random server port. The web tests build their assets before checking all four pages and the JavaScript/CSS bundles. Build manually with `npm run build`; esbuild bundles `src/web/*.js` into `dist/` and copies HTML/CSS.

## Shopping

Browse and filter the catalog at `/`, see details at `/product.html?id=mug-classic`, edit your cart at `/cart.html`, and finish at `/checkout.html`. The browser keeps its cart id in localStorage. Carts are held in server memory and reset on restart. Checkout snapshots names/prices into persistent orders and serializes stock writes so the last unit can sell only once within a server process.

The committed seed has 30 products across five categories, including an unavailable notebook and a single canvas tote. Try `WELCOME10` (10% off), `SAVE500` (500 cents off a subtotal of at least 2000 cents), or `CAP` (a fixed discount capped at the subtotal). Tax is 8% after discounts, rounded half up.

## Admin

Set `ADMIN_TOKEN` before starting: `ADMIN_TOKEN=your-secret npm start`. Every admin call requires `x-admin-token: your-secret`; without an environment token, admin access is disabled. Keep this token private.

Admin endpoints are `POST /api/admin/products`, `PATCH /api/admin/products/:id`, and `GET /api/admin/orders`. A product requires id, name, description, priceCents, category, stock, and imageUrl. Categories must already occur in the catalog; ids are unique and cannot be patched. Order listing returns an array, newest first.

Example: `curl -H "x-admin-token: your-secret" http://localhost:3000/api/admin/orders`.

## API and persistence

Health is `GET /health`. Products and categories are under `/api/products` and `/api/categories`; carts under `/api/carts`; checkout is `POST /api/checkout` with `{ "cartId": "…", "email": "you@example.com" }`; read a saved order at `GET /api/orders/:id`. Errors use `{ "error": { "code": "…", "message": "…" } }`.

Products, discounts and orders live under `data/`. Each write creates a temporary file and renames it into place. `data/orders.json` is created on the first successful checkout. Run one server process per data directory; the checkout lock is process-local. Individual JSON writes are atomic; there is no cross-file crash transaction. The server exports `createApp({ dataDir })` for integration tests.

`.gitignore` excludes node_modules, dist, coverage and logs from Git. LayerFS still stores them; `.lww` imports those generated-path merge rules.
